claim: to revert to the original mode, type this: printf '\033[0;37;40m\n'
quote: HOWTO Introduction tells the reader to revert with echo "^[[0;37;40m" (ESC then [0;37;40m). That is the same SGR sequence printf '\033[0;37;40m\n' sends; clear(1) HTML likewise documents printf with \033[…] escapes.
earlier: From the HOWTO alone I would have said disagrees because it prints echo, not printf; the shared escape sequence makes the printf form equivalent.

claim: control characters like suspend (CTRL-Z), interrupt and quit (CTRL-C)
quote: HOWTO names suspend (CTRL-Z), interrupt and quit (CTRL-C). man/curs_inopts.3x likewise discusses the interrupt, quit, suspend, and flow-control characters for cbreak vs raw.
earlier: Same after the man page; the HOWTO later misstates cbreak handling, but that is outside this claim fragment.

claim: Other border functions draws lines with them (the forms-drawing characters)
quote: HOWTO §9.5 says mvhline/mvvline create a horizontal or vertical line of the specified length; the example draws with ASCII '|','-','+', not ACS forms-drawing. man/curs_border.3x: forms-drawing characters are used when a border argument is 0, not that 'other border functions' inherently draw with them. Grammar: 'draws' disagrees with plural subject.
earlier: After only the HOWTO section I already had disagrees (ASCII example, no forms-drawing claim).

claim: Initially the terminal has echoing enabled and is in ordinary cooked mode, so one or the other has to be changed before calling getch(); otherwise, the program's output will be unpredictable
quote: ncurses-intro Input: 'Since initially the terminal has echoing enabled and is in ordinary cooked mode, one or the other has to changed before calling getch(); otherwise, the program's output will be unpredictable.' Substance matches; man pages require cbreak/raw for interactive getch with echo.
earlier: Matches after the intro alone; man pages only confirm.

claim: While getnstr() is reading the line, F1 is ignored, like the other function keys
quote: wgetnstr discards most function keys with beep(); KEY_F(1) is KEY_MIN-class and takes the discard/beep path. Not all keys are ignored: KEY_LEFT/KEY_BACKSPACE erase; KEY_DOWN/KEY_ENTER terminate. 'Ignored' is loose (beep), but F1 is not inserted.
earlier: From the man page alone I nearly said disagrees because discards call beep and some KEY_* are handled; source confirms F1 is discarded.

claim: Fifth is the color index. It is the index given during init_pair()
quote: HOWTO chgat comment calls the fifth argument 'the color index'. man/curs_attr.3x: 'the color pair argument is a color pair index (as in the first argument of init_pair)'. Color index in curs_color is a palette color (COLOR_*), not the pair number.
earlier: HOWTO alone would match the claim to itself; the man page supplies the contradiction.

claim: Do this before the next wgetch(); otherwise another mouse event might come in and make the first one inaccessible
quote: ncurses-intro: call getmouse() 'before the next wgetch(), otherwise another mouse event might come in and make the first one inaccessible.' getmouse man: removes the event from the queue.
earlier: Matches from the intro alone.

claim: An example showing all the characters, with 31 SHOW() lines and no ACS_URCORNER
quote: HOWTO: 'Here is an example showing all the characters.' The ACS example has exactly 31 SHOW() lines (UL/LL/LR corners, etc.) and never references ACS_URCORNER, which exists in curses.h/man as the upper-right corner.
earlier: Counting SHOW lines alone suggested matches as a description; ACS_URCORNER in the headers shows 'all the characters' is false.

claim: Note that new_field() does not copy the pointer array into private storage
quote: Intro attributes the non-copying of the FIELD** array to new_field(), but the preceding API is new_form(FIELD **fields). new_form stores form->field = fields without copying; new_field() does not take a pointer array.
earlier: Intro wording alone looked self-consistent until compared with new_form's signature and Connect_Fields.

claim: By default, all options are on.
quote: Intro: 'By default, all options are on.' man/form_field_opts.3x: standard options 'all are on by default'; extension options 'are off by default'. default_field.opts is STD_FIELD_OPTS.
earlier: Matches the intro; the man page narrows 'all' to standard options, so confidence drops from high.

claim: Each field structure contains one character pointer slot ... The (char *) type is retained for System V compatibility
quote: Intro still shows char *userptr and says '(char *) type is retained for System V compatibility.' Current man and fld_user.c use void *userptr / void *usrptr.
earlier: Intro alone would match; headers/man show the retained char* claim is outdated.

claim: The growth limit can be changed whether or not the O_STATIC bit is on, but has no effect until it is.
quote: Intro repeats the claim. set_max_field stores maxgrow always, but sets _MAY_GROW only when O_STATIC is off. O_STATIC on means fixed buffers; growth applies when O_STATIC is off. As written, 'until it is' (on) is the wrong polarity.
earlier: Ambiguous intro sentence suggested can't tell; fld_max.c settles that growth is active only with O_STATIC off.

claim: A REQ_MOVE_RIGHT from A will go to B
quote: Intro: 'A REQ_MOVE_RIGHT from A will go to B only if A, B, and C all share the same first line; otherwise it will skip over B to C.' Field ordering uses frow/fcol. The absolute claim omits the required condition.
earlier: Same after reading the full intro sentence with the condition.

claim: the position of a form for purposes of these requests is its upper-left corner
quote: Intro says the position of a form is its upper-left corner for visual field moves. Insert_Field_By_Position compares each field's frow/fcol — field corners, not a form object position.
earlier: Intro alone would match; driver/sort code shows 'form' should be 'field'.

claim: REQ_DEL_PREV: Delete previous word at cursor.
quote: Intro lists REQ_DEL_PREV as 'Delete previous word at cursor.' man/form_driver.3x: 'Delete character before the cursor.' form.h: 'delete char before cursor.' FE_Delete_Previous deletes the previous character; REQ_DEL_WORD deletes a word.
earlier: Intro alone would match; man/header/driver contradict 'word'.

claim: When the current page is changed by set_current_field() call; When the current field is changed by a set_form_page() call
quote: Intro swaps the APIs: set_current_field sets the current field; set_form_page sets the form's page. The printed pairing of page↔set_current_field and field↔set_form_page is reversed.
earlier: Same after man/form_page.3x.

claim: ncurses is intended to be base-level conformant with the X/Open Curses standard ... almost all the features not directly concerned with wide characters and internationalization
quote: ncurses-intro XSI Curses Conformance: 'intended to be base-level conformant with the XSI Curses standard from X/Open. Many extended-level features (in fact, almost all features not directly concerned with wide characters and internationalization) are also supported.'
earlier: Matches from the intro section alone.

claim: Slide the tiles with the arrow keys until they're in order
quote: HOWTO Shuffle section only says 'A fun game, if you have time to kill' and cites JustForFun/shuffle.c. No shuffle.c appears under primary evidence paths (ncurses/,form/,menu/,panel/,progs/,include/,Ada95/,c++/,misc/,man/,doc/html/, INSTALL/NEWS/README/ANNOUNCE).
earlier: Missing sample would have been 'missing'; without the program source the tile-sliding instructions cannot be checked.

claim: [pads](glossary/pad.md) stdscr with blanks: the glossary link was on the verb
quote: Intro: resizeterm 'pads stdscr with blanks if the screen is larger' — pads is a verb. A pad window is a different concept (resizeterm: 'It is not possible to automatically resize pads.'). Whether the edition linked glossary/pad.md is outside primary evidence (appears_in is corrected text, not evidence).
earlier: Technical 'pads stdscr with blanks' matches; the glossary-link placement needs the edition shard, which is not primary evidence.

claim: ncurses also uses the parameter's absolute value as the number of lines to take, and the binding's Rip_Off_Lines routine relies on this.
quote: Public ripoffline() collapses the argument to ±1, but _nc_ripoffline stores the full value and later uses count = abs(line) when creating the ripped window. Ada Rip_Off_Lines imports _nc_ripoffline and documents that absolute value.
earlier: man/curs_kernel.3x alone (one line only) would suggest disagrees; _nc_ripoffline and the Ada binding confirm the claim.

claim: parse an entire terminfo file into a doubly-linked circular list of entry structures
quote: Hackguide says doubly-linked circular list. ENTRY has next/last (doubly linked), but enqueue sets tail->next = NULL and the entries.c diagram shows NULL ends — a linear list, not circular.
earlier: Hackguide alone would match; enqueue/entries.c refute 'circular'.

claim: This, for example, is where the AIX box1 capability gets translated to an acsc string.
quote: Hackguide points at parse_entry translation of AIX box1 to acsc. parse_entry.c: 'Translate AIX forms characters' from box_chars_1 into acs_chars with warning 'acsc string synthesized from AIX capabilities'.
earlier: Matches after hackguide; source confirms.

claim: The tput and clear utilities just do an entry load followed by a tputs() of a selected capability.
quote: Hackguide states that simplification. clear_cmd uses tputs(clear_screen, …) (and optional E3). tput calls setupterm then capability output — more than a single tputs, but the core path matches the description.
earlier: Hackguide alone would be high; reading tput.c shows more command handling, so medium.

claim: and also interprets the contents of the $TERM environment variable
quote: INSTALL §2 with --enable-termcap: 'the library will search /etc/termcap before the terminfo database, and will also interpret the contents of the $TERM environment variable.'
earlier: Matches from INSTALL alone (in the enable-termcap paragraph).

claim: $(prefix)/man: the manual pages
quote: INSTALL: 'Under $(prefix)/man: the manual pages' among the install layout entries.
earlier: Matches from INSTALL alone.

claim: The color pair is stored with the attributes, and the wide-character functions use the attr_t type and names such as attr_on().
quote: COLOR_PAIR can be or'd into attributes; attr_t can hold a color pair in A_COLOR. Wide API includes attr_on/wattr_on taking attr_t.
earlier: Matches after curs_attr.3x.

claim: most are named by adding _w to the 8-bit name, so waddch() becomes wadd_wch()
quote: man/ncurses.3x: where a non-wide name contains 'ch' or 'str', prefix with '_w'; example 'waddch becomes wadd_wch'.
earlier: Matches from ncurses.3x alone.

claim: the library searches /etc/termcap before the terminfo database
quote: INSTALL: with --enable-termcap, 'the library will search /etc/termcap before the terminfo database'.
earlier: Matches from INSTALL (enable-termcap context).
